subject: humanities
passage: Papua New Guinea, which occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea, is one of the most linguistically diverse places on Earth. Many of its valleys are separated by steep mountains and dense forest, so neighboring communities developed their own ways of speaking over thousands of years. Today, the number of distinct languages used across the country ______ more than 800, according to most estimates, and many of them are spoken by only a few thousand people.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: The subject is "the number," which is singular; "of distinct languages used across the country" describes it. "The number of" takes a singular verb, and "Today" calls for the present tense, so "is" is correct.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Are" is plural and seems to agree with "languages," but the subject is the singular "number."
explanation.B: Correct. The singular present-tense verb "is" agrees with "the number" and fits "Today."
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Were" is plural, but the subject "number" is singular; it is also past tense, which conflicts with "Today."
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Have been" is plural, but the subject "number" is singular.
